title: Trent Posts 22% Profit Rise as Zudio and Westside Expansion Drives Growth
excerpt: The Tata Group retailer's first-quarter earnings beat estimates on the back of aggressive store rollouts into smaller Indian cities, though rising raw material costs remain a headwind.
body:
• Trent's Q1 FY27 net profit rose 22% year-on-year to ₹5.19 billion ($54.5 million), driven by store expansion beyond metropolitan cities.
  • Revenue climbed to ₹57.55 billion from ₹48.83 billion in the year-ago quarter, roughly an 18% increase.
  • The company added 1 Westside and 19 Zudio stores during the quarter, taking its total footprint to 1,312 outlets across India and the UAE.
  • Rising raw material costs partially offset the growth, keeping margins under pressure.

Indian retailer Trent on Thursday reported a 22 percent rise in first-quarter profit, as aggressive expansion of its Westside and Zudio apparel brands into smaller cities helped outweigh pressure from rising raw material costs.

The Tata Group firm's standalone net profit rose to 5.19 billion rupees ($54.51 million) for the quarter ended June 30, up from 4.25 billion rupees a year earlier. Revenue climbed to 57.55 billion rupees from 48.83 billion rupees.

The Zudio Growth Engine

Trent's value-fashion chain Zudio continues to be the primary growth driver. The company added 19 Zudio stores during the quarter, taking its total Zudio network to 982 outlets — including seven in the United Arab Emirates, the brand's first international footprint. A single Westside store was also added, bringing that chain to 301 locations.

As of June 30, Trent operated 1,312 stores in total, including 29 outlets under other lifestyle formats. The company's strategy of expanding into tier-2 and tier-3 cities is tapping a rising demand for branded, affordable fashion outside India's metropolitan centres.

Revenue Beats Earlier Estimates

The full quarterly results topped Trent's own preliminary business update from early July, which had pegged standalone revenue at 56.66 billion rupees — a 19 percent increase. The final number came in slightly higher at 57.55 billion rupees, suggesting stronger-than-expected footfall and same-store performance in the closing weeks of the quarter.

Brokerages remain bullish. HSBC had expected roughly 21 percent revenue growth for the quarter, while Bernstein recently noted that faster Westside expansion could provide an additional growth driver alongside Zudio.

Cost Pressures Linger

Despite the top-line strength, rising input costs — particularly in cotton and synthetic textiles — ate into margins. The gap between revenue growth and profit growth suggests that Trent is absorbing some cost inflation rather than passing it fully to consumers, a strategic choice to protect Zudio's value positioning.

ICICI Direct estimates Trent's revenue, EBITDA and net profit to grow at compound annual rates of roughly 23, 25 and 22 percent respectively through FY28, with EBITDA margins expanding from about 18.5 percent in FY26 to 19.1 percent by FY28.

Investor Takeaway

Trent's results confirm it remains one of the strongest performers in Indian retail. The company's ability to maintain double-digit profit growth while expanding aggressively — and while navigating elevated input costs — sets it apart from peers. The UAE expansion of Zudio is a signal worth watching: if the brand's affordable-fashion formula translates internationally, it could open a significant new growth runway.

For investors tracking India's consumer story, Trent's Q1 numbers reinforce the thesis that organised retail is steadily taking share from the unorganised sector, particularly in smaller cities where branded alternatives were previously scarce.
